text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Insurance payment officers are to make more home visits and not only to people who are sick in a crackdown on false claims. This is a proposition that will be put to parliament on Thursday.

- Swedish textile companies are moving production centres eastwards into the Baltic states to save money on labour. The number of people employed in the textile and clothing industry in Sweden has fallen about 100,000 since 1950.

- Swedish membership in the European economic and monetary union(EMU) would be stabilising for the Sweden economy, said Lars Jacobsson, the head of the Swedish Retail and Wholesale Research Institute HUI. He forecast the gap between Swedish and German yields will grow this autumn with increased uncertainty on the way if Sweden stays outside the EMU.
- Insurer Skandia's 1996 profit was hit by a restructuring cost of 1.4 billion crowns. Its pre-tax profit was 1.65 billion crowns in 1996 against 1.55 billion in 1995.
- Sweden's white collar workers' union, SIF, has flatly turned down a suggestion by the academics group Saco to cooperate on wages.

- Swedish Information Technology company Euroseek Inc is to seek its fortune on New York's Nasdaq exchange. The company has developed a search engine for the Internet. It plans to hold an issue of five million shares worth 60 cents each over the Internet and seek listing on Nasdaq. The issue represents 20 percent of the company's votes and capital.

- Swedish Retail and Wholesale Research Institute HUI forecasts retail sales will experience a new upswing. While 1997 is seen as a middle year, 1998 is expected to see a pick-up in Sweden's home market with private consumption growing up to two percent and Gross Domestic Product rising over three percent.

- European investors could be in for a very positive development in the second half of this year, according to Felix Zulauf, the man behind the investment bank Merrill Lynch's recently started European Equities Fund. Speaking at an investor seminar in Gothenburg, Zulauf predicted that after a downturn of 10-12 percent in the second quarter of 1997, European stock markets will rally maybe 25-30 percent.
- The Swedish Labour Board, AMS, is preparing to launch a comprehensive nationwide job placement service on the Internet. Potential employers will be able to surf the net looking for the right staff.

- Employees at Volvo's assembly plant in Gent, Belgium will walk off their jobs on Friday in sympathy with their Belgian colleagues at the Renault factory in Vilvoorde which is being closed with the loss of up to 3,100 jobs.
- Swedish industrial engineer Atlas Copco has reached a preliminary agreement to acquire Thome-Crepelle, a French compressor company, from Five-Lile.
